# 1 Kings Chapter 11 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Now King Solomon loved many foreign women, along with the daughter of Pharaoh: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women,
**2** from the nations concerning which the LORD had said to the people of Israel, "You shall not enter into marriage with them, neither shall they with you, for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods." Solomon clung to these in love.
**3** He had seven hundred wives, who were princesses, and three hundred concubines. And his wives turned away his heart.
**4** For when Solomon was old his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not wholly true to the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
**5** For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
**6** So Solomon did what was evil in the sight of the LORD and did not wholly follow the LORD, as David his father had done.
**7** Then Solomon built a high place for Chemosh the abomination of Moab, on the mountain east of Jerusalem, and for Molech the abomination of the Ammonites.
**8** And so he did for all his foreign wives, who made offerings and sacrificed to their gods.
**9** And the LORD was angry with Solomon, because his heart had turned away from the LORD, the God of Israel, who had appeared to him twice
**10** and had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods. But he did not keep what the LORD commanded.
**11** Therefore the LORD said to Solomon, "Since this has been your practice and you have not kept my covenant and my statutes that I commanded you, I will surely tear the kingdom from you and will give it to your servant.
**12** Yet for the sake of David your father I will not do it in your days, but I will tear it out of the hand of your son.
**13** However, I will not tear away all the kingdom, but I will give one tribe to your son, for the sake of David my servant and for the sake of Jerusalem that I have chosen."
**14** And the LORD raised up an adversary against Solomon, Hadad the Edomite. He was of the royal house in Edom.
**15** For when David was in Edom, and Joab the commander of the army went up to bury the slain, he struck down every male in Edom.
**16** For six months Joab and all Israel remained there, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
**17** But Hadad fled to Egypt, together with certain Edomites of his father's servants, Hadad being yet a little child.
**18** They set out from Midian and came to Paran and took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house and assigned him an allowance of food and gave him land.
**19** And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him in marriage the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
**20** And the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's house. And Genubath was in Pharaoh's house among the sons of Pharaoh.
**21** But when Hadad heard in Egypt that David slept with his fathers and that Joab the commander of the army was dead, Hadad said to Pharaoh, "Let me depart, that I may go to my own country."
**22** But Pharaoh said to him, "What have you lacked with me that you are now seeking to go to your own country?" And he said to him, "Only let me go."
**23** God also raised up as an adversary to him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.
**24** And he gathered men about him and became leader of a marauding band, after the killing by David. And they went to Damascus and lived there and made him king in Damascus.
**25** He was an adversary of Israel all the days of Solomon, doing harm as Hadad did. And he loathed Israel and reigned over Syria.
**26** Jeroboam the son of Nebat, an Ephraimite of Zeredah, a servant of Solomon, whose mother's name was Zeruah, a widow, also lifted up his hand against the king.
**27** And this was the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon built the Millo and closed up the breach of the city of David his father.
**28** The man Jeroboam was very able, and when Solomon saw that the young man was industrious, he gave him charge over all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
**29** And at that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road. Now Ahijah had dressed himself in a new garment, and the two of them were alone in the open country.
**30** Then Ahijah laid hold of the new garment that was on him, and tore it into twelve pieces.
**31** And he said to Jeroboam, "Take for yourself ten pieces, for thus says the LORD, the God of Israel, 'Behold, I am about to tear the kingdom from the hand of Solomon and will give you ten tribes.
**32** But he shall have one tribe, for the sake of my servant David and for the sake of Jerusalem, the city that I have chosen out of all the tribes of Israel,
**33** because they have forsaken me and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites, and they have not walked in my ways, doing what is right in my sight and keeping my statutes and my rules, as David his father did.
**34** Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, but I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my statutes.
**35** But I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand and will give it to you, ten tribes.
**36** Yet to his son I will give one tribe, that David my servant may always have a lamp before me in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to put my name.
**37** And I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.
**38** And if you will listen to all that I command you, and will walk in my ways, and do what is right in my sight by keeping my statutes and my commandments, as David my servant did, I will be with you and will build you a sure house, as I built for David, and I will give Israel to you.
**39** And I will afflict the offspring of David because of this, but not forever.'"
**40** Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled into Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
**41** Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
**42** And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
**43** And Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father. And Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.

---
## Council Notes

SOPHIA has reviewed the translations of EMET (literal), LOGOS (formal), and PNEUMA (dynamic) for this chapter.

**Method**: Each verse was compared across all three translations. The LOGOS formal translation serves as the primary consensus baseline, with adjustments where EMET's literalism reveals important Hebrew features or PNEUMA's dynamic rendering better captures the original intent.

**Key Observations**:
- EMET preserves Hebrew word order and particles (ʾet, vav-consecutive) that reveal syntactic emphasis
- LOGOS provides the most balanced English rendering suitable for study
- PNEUMA's dynamic approach often captures emotional register and narrative pacing most effectively

## ⚠️ Disagreement Log

**Chapter 11**: 29 verse(s) with significant divergence

### Verse 1
- **EMET**: And-the-king Solomon loved many foreign women — and-the-daughter-of Pharaoh — Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and-Hittite —
- **LOGOS**: Now King Solomon loved many foreign women, along with the daughter of Pharaoh: Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women,
- **PNEUMA**: King Solomon loved many foreign women besides Pharaoh's daughter — women from Moab, Ammon, Edom, Sidon, and the Hittites.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 2
- **EMET**: from the-nations of-which YHWH said to the-sons-of Israel, "You-shall-not go among-them and-they shall-not go among-you; surely they-will-turn ʾet-your-heart after their-gods." To-them Solomon clung i...
- **LOGOS**: from the nations concerning which the LORD had said to the people of Israel, "You shall not enter into marriage with them, neither shall they with you, for surely they will turn away your heart after ...
- **PNEUMA**: They came from the very nations about which the LORD had told the Israelites, "You must not intermarry with them, because they will surely turn your hearts to their gods." Yet Solomon held fast to the...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 3
- **EMET**: And-he-had wives — princesses: seven hundred; and-concubines: three hundred. And-his-wives turned ʾet-his-heart.
- **LOGOS**: He had seven hundred wives, who were princesses, and three hundred concubines. And his wives turned away his heart.
- **PNEUMA**: He had seven hundred wives of royal birth and three hundred concubines — and his wives led his heart astray.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 4
- **EMET**: And-it-was at-the-time-of the-old-age-of Solomon, his-wives turned ʾet-his-heart after other gods, and-his-heart was-not complete with YHWH his-God, as the-heart-of David his-father.
- **LOGOS**: For when Solomon was old his wives turned away his heart after other gods, and his heart was not wholly true to the LORD his God, as was the heart of David his father.
- **PNEUMA**: As Solomon grew old, his wives turned his heart toward other gods. His heart was no longer fully devoted to the LORD his God, as his father David's heart had been.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 5
- **EMET**: And-Solomon went after Ashtoreth, the-goddess-of the-Sidonians, and-after Milcom, the-abomination-of the-Ammonites.
- **LOGOS**: For Solomon went after Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, and after Milcom the abomination of the Ammonites.
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon followed Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians and Milcom the detestable god of the Ammonites.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 8
- **EMET**: And-so he-did for-all his-foreign wives, who-burned-incense and-sacrificed to-their-gods.
- **LOGOS**: And so he did for all his foreign wives, who made offerings and sacrificed to their gods.
- **PNEUMA**: He did the same for all his foreign wives, who burned incense and offered sacrifices to their gods.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 10
- **EMET**: and-had-commanded-him concerning this thing, not to-go after other gods. But-he-did-not keep ʾet-what YHWH commanded.
- **LOGOS**: and had commanded him concerning this thing, that he should not go after other gods. But he did not keep what the LORD commanded.
- **PNEUMA**: and had specifically warned him about this very thing — not to follow other gods. But Solomon refused to obey.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 16
- **EMET**: for six months Joab dwelt there, and-all Israel, until he-had-cut-off every male in-Edom —
- **LOGOS**: For six months Joab and all Israel remained there, until he had cut off every male in Edom.
- **PNEUMA**: Joab and all the Israelites stayed there six months, until they had killed every male.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 17
- **EMET**: and-Hadad fled, he and-certain Edomite men from-the-servants-of his-father with-him, to-go to-Egypt. And-Hadad was a-small youth.
- **LOGOS**: But Hadad fled to Egypt, together with certain Edomites of his father's servants, Hadad being yet a little child.
- **PNEUMA**: But Hadad, still a young boy, escaped to Egypt with some of his father's Edomite officials.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 18
- **EMET**: And-they-arose from-Midian and-came to-Paran, and-they-took men with-them from-Paran and-came to-Egypt, to-Pharaoh king-of Egypt, and-he-gave to-him a-house and-food he-assigned to-him and-land he-gav...
- **LOGOS**: They set out from Midian and came to Paran and took men with them from Paran and came to Egypt, to Pharaoh king of Egypt, who gave him a house and assigned him an allowance of food and gave him land.
- **PNEUMA**: They left Midian, traveled through Paran, picked up more men along the way, and arrived in Egypt. Pharaoh gave Hadad a house, a food allowance, and land.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 19
- **EMET**: And-Hadad found great favor in-the-eyes-of Pharaoh, and-he-gave to-him a-wife — the-sister-of his-own-wife, the-sister-of Tahpenes the-queen.
- **LOGOS**: And Hadad found great favor in the sight of Pharaoh, so that he gave him in marriage the sister of his own wife, the sister of Tahpenes the queen.
- **PNEUMA**: Hadad gained such favor with Pharaoh that the king gave him his wife's sister — Queen Tahpenes's sister — in marriage.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 20
- **EMET**: And-the-sister-of Tahpenes bore to-him ʾet-Genubath his-son, and-Tahpenes weaned-him in-the-midst-of the-house-of Pharaoh. And-Genubath was in-the-house-of Pharaoh among the-sons-of Pharaoh.
- **LOGOS**: And the sister of Tahpenes bore him Genubath his son, whom Tahpenes weaned in Pharaoh's house. And Genubath was in Pharaoh's house among the sons of Pharaoh.
- **PNEUMA**: Tahpenes's sister bore him a son, Genubath, whom Tahpenes raised in the palace alongside Pharaoh's own children.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 22
- **EMET**: And-Pharaoh said to-him, "But what are-you lacking with-me, that behold, you are-seeking to-go to your-land?" And-he-said, "Nothing, but sending you-must-send-me."
- **LOGOS**: But Pharaoh said to him, "What have you lacked with me that you are now seeking to go to your own country?" And he said to him, "Only let me go."
- **PNEUMA**: "What have you lacked here that makes you want to leave?" Pharaoh asked. "Nothing," Hadad replied, "but please let me go."
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 23
- **EMET**: And-God raised-up to-him an-adversary — Rezon son-of Eliada, who had-fled from Hadadezer king-of Zobah, his-master.
- **LOGOS**: God also raised up as an adversary to him, Rezon the son of Eliada, who had fled from his master Hadadezer king of Zobah.
- **PNEUMA**: God also raised up another adversary against Solomon — Rezon son of Eliada, who had deserted his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 24
- **EMET**: And-he-gathered to-himself men and-became commander-of a-raiding-band when-David killed-them. And-they-went to-Damascus and-dwelt in-it and-reigned in-Damascus.
- **LOGOS**: And he gathered men about him and became leader of a marauding band, after the killing by David. And they went to Damascus and lived there and made him king in Damascus.
- **PNEUMA**: After David's victories, Rezon gathered a band of rebels and went to Damascus, where they settled and he became king.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 25
- **EMET**: And-he-was an-adversary to-Israel all the-days-of Solomon — and-the-evil that Hadad did — and-he-loathed Israel and-reigned over Aram.
- **LOGOS**: He was an adversary of Israel all the days of Solomon, doing harm as Hadad did. And he loathed Israel and reigned over Syria.
- **PNEUMA**: Rezon was hostile to Israel throughout Solomon's reign, compounding the trouble caused by Hadad. He ruled over Aram and was a constant threat to Israel.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 27
- **EMET**: And-this is the-matter why he-raised a-hand against the-king: Solomon built ʾet-the-Millo; he-closed ʾet-the-breach-of the-City-of David his-father.
- **LOGOS**: And this was the reason why he lifted up his hand against the king. Solomon built the Millo and closed up the breach of the city of David his father.
- **PNEUMA**: This is the story of his rebellion: Solomon was building the Millo, closing the gap in the wall of the City of David.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 28
- **EMET**: And-the-man Jeroboam was a-mighty-man-of valor. And-Solomon saw the-young-man that he was doing work, and-he-appointed-him over all the-forced-labor-of the-house-of Joseph.
- **LOGOS**: The man Jeroboam was very able, and when Solomon saw that the young man was industrious, he gave him charge over all the forced labor of the house of Joseph.
- **PNEUMA**: Jeroboam was an exceptionally capable man. When Solomon noticed how industrious this young man was, he put him in charge of the entire labor force of the tribes of Joseph.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 29
- **EMET**: And-it-was at-that time, and-Jeroboam went-out from-Jerusalem, and-Ahijah the-Shilonite, the-prophet, found-him on-the-way, and-he was-clothed with-a-new garment. And-the-two-of-them were alone in-the...
- **LOGOS**: And at that time, when Jeroboam went out of Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah the Shilonite found him on the road. Now Ahijah had dressed himself in a new garment, and the two of them were alone in the op...
- **PNEUMA**: One day, as Jeroboam was leaving Jerusalem, the prophet Ahijah of Shiloh met him on the road. Ahijah was wearing a new cloak, and the two of them were alone in the countryside.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 30
- **EMET**: And-Ahijah seized the-new garment that was upon-him, and-tore-it — twelve pieces.
- **LOGOS**: Then Ahijah laid hold of the new garment that was on him, and tore it into twelve pieces.
- **PNEUMA**: Ahijah grabbed the new cloak he was wearing and ripped it into twelve pieces.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 33
- **EMET**: Because they-forsook-me and-bowed-down to-Ashtoreth goddess-of the-Sidonians, to-Chemosh god-of Moab, and-to-Milcom god-of the-sons-of Ammon, and-did-not walk in-my-ways, to-do the-right in-my-eyes an...
- **LOGOS**: because they have forsaken me and worshiped Ashtoreth the goddess of the Sidonians, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of the Ammonites, and they have not walked in my ways, doing what is rig...
- **PNEUMA**: I am doing this because they have abandoned me and worshiped Ashtoreth goddess of Sidon, Chemosh god of Moab, and Milcom god of Ammon. They have not walked in my ways or done what is right in my eyes ...
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 34
- **EMET**: And-I-will-not take ʾet-all the-kingdom from-his-hand, for prince I-will-set-him all the-days-of his-life, for-the-sake-of David my-servant whom I-chose, who kept my-commandments and-my-statutes.
- **LOGOS**: Nevertheless, I will not take the whole kingdom out of his hand, but I will make him ruler all the days of his life, for the sake of David my servant whom I chose, who kept my commandments and my stat...
- **PNEUMA**: But I will not take the whole kingdom from Solomon. I will let him be ruler for the rest of his life, for the sake of my servant David, whom I chose because he obeyed my commands and decrees.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 35
- **EMET**: And-I-will-take the-kingdom from-the-hand-of his-son, and-give-it to-you — ʾet-the-ten tribes.
- **LOGOS**: But I will take the kingdom out of his son's hand and will give it to you, ten tribes.
- **PNEUMA**: I will take the kingdom from his son and give you ten tribes.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 37
- **EMET**: And-you I-will-take, and-you-will-reign over all that your-soul desires, and-you-will-be king over Israel.
- **LOGOS**: And I will take you, and you shall reign over all that your soul desires, and you shall be king over Israel.
- **PNEUMA**: As for you, I will take you, and you will rule over everything your heart desires. You will be king over Israel.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 39
- **EMET**: And-I-will-afflict ʾet-the-seed-of David because-of this — only not all the-days.'"
- **LOGOS**: And I will afflict the offspring of David because of this, but not forever.'"
- **PNEUMA**: I will humble David's descendants because of this — but not forever.'"
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 40
- **EMET**: And-Solomon sought to-kill ʾet-Jeroboam. And-Jeroboam arose and-fled to-Egypt, to Shishak king-of Egypt, and-he-was in-Egypt until the-death-of Solomon.
- **LOGOS**: Solomon sought therefore to kill Jeroboam. But Jeroboam arose and fled into Egypt, to Shishak king of Egypt, and was in Egypt until the death of Solomon.
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon tried to kill Jeroboam, but Jeroboam fled to Egypt, to King Shishak, and stayed there until Solomon died.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 41
- **EMET**: And-the-rest-of the-acts-of Solomon, and-all that he-did, and-his-wisdom — are-they not written in-the-Book-of the-Acts-of Solomon?
- **LOGOS**: Now the rest of the acts of Solomon, and all that he did, and his wisdom, are they not written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon?
- **PNEUMA**: As for the rest of Solomon's reign — everything he did and the wisdom he showed — it is all recorded in the Book of the Acts of Solomon.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 42
- **EMET**: And-the-days that Solomon reigned in-Jerusalem over all Israel were forty years.
- **LOGOS**: And the time that Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel was forty years.
- **PNEUMA**: Solomon reigned in Jerusalem over all Israel for forty years.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

### Verse 43
- **EMET**: And-Solomon lay-down with his-fathers, and-was-buried in-the-City-of David his-father. And-Rehoboam his-son reigned in-his-place.
- **LOGOS**: And Solomon slept with his fathers and was buried in the city of David his father. And Rehoboam his son reigned in his place.
- **PNEUMA**: Then Solomon died and was buried in the City of David. His son Rehoboam succeeded him as king.
- **SOPHIA ruling**: LOGOS rendering adopted as consensus with minor adjustments.

— SOPHIA
